summary: Analysis only, no compiler commits. Worktree famlan at famk ce83370, libs built, fresh uc80 run of all 112 programs in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wohl-src-uc80/ec4c5501-bd11-4fd4-8f7f-ed83b93def9a/scratchpad/faml_an/fresh.csv (104 OK, 3 FITS, 5 TOO-BIG, same as the committed results). The fresh uc80 numbers equal the family K report: 10 programs bigger than SDCC 4.6.0 size mode (davidly-e +9, dhrystone21 +89/+111/+81, mojozork-size +924, sort-equ-5000 +386, sort-ord-5000 +384, sort-rev-5000 +385, sort-ran-5000 +541, sort-ran-20 +96) and 2 programs slower than SDCC speed mode: davidly-ttt 8,239,388 vs 7,960,572 T (1.035) and micro+loop 1,256,037 vs 1,102,397 T (1.139). Fresh SDCC rebuilds of davidly-e, dhrystone21, mojozork, sort-ran-5000, micro+loop and davidly-ttt reproduce the committed SDCC rows exactly (a full SDCC rerun was stopped: single sdcc compiles take minutes under load). Every gap was attributed with function-level listings and closed in measurement by hand-edited .mac files, a replacement library module or a source rewrite, with golden checks (ab.py runs the check and time builds, z88dk-ticks region counts). Measured result: all 10 size gaps and both speed gaps flip to a win with zero T loss on the timed regions, except the optional --size-helpers route. Largest levers: (1) one-assignment static pointer constant folding plus (&obj)->f folding (mojozork -3531 B), (2) a word qsort __qsort_wr (332 B) with a register-convention comparator (the 8 sort programs shrink 7514 -> 4522 B, T -17% to -54%), (3) deletion of calls to empty functions (mojozork -1259 B), (4) merging x / y with x % y into one divide (davidly-e 498 -> 466 B and -38% T), (5) mul16c at loop depth 1 in call-heavy loops (dhrystone -116 B each, T -0.03%), (6) register convention for external asm functions such as out() and in() (ROM kernels -35 to -167 B and -5% to -17% T). The ROM kernels lose to an SDCC ROM build today (cmdq 1475 B / 7.87M T against 1188 B size mode and 7.09M T speed mode); item 6 plus small items flips T on all four and size on ymreg and seq, and cmdq/fnum stay 50-70 B over until further small items land. Scratch tools and measurements are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wohl-src-uc80/ec4c5501-bd11-4fd4-8f7f-ed83b93def9a/scratchpad/faml_an.

size_gaps.causes: Divide helpers: __sdiv16 35 + __smod16 35 + __div16 87 + __dv8n 47 = 204 B against 134 B for SDCC (__divsint, __modsint, __divuint, __get_remainder, ___sdcc_enter_ix). Console: __conout 53 B + __puts_s 28 B against SDCC putchar 23 + puts 29 (SDCC also links a dead getchar 23 B and gsinit 37 B). main is 187 B against 218 B, so uc80 is 31 B smaller there. Two statements compute x % n and then x / n with equal operands, so the loop pays for two divides per pass. The register-locals pass keeps N, x and n in memory (UC80_RL_DEBUG: n and x rejected in BC with 'read of the local after a clobber', DE has negative gain), and the loop start n = N - 1 is not folded to 199 although N is a known constant there.
size_gaps.fix: (1) Merge a pair x / y and x % y with equal pure operands (no store to x or y between) into one call of a new __sdivmod16 (58 B, replaces __sdiv16 + __smod16 = 70 B, quotient in HL, remainder in DE, signs handled). (2) Propagate the local constant into the for init (n = 199). (3) Rewrite __conout in 42 B with the same CR/LF behaviour. (4) Peephole 'ld HL,(x) / ex DE,HL / ld HL,(y)' to 'ld DE,(x)' when HL still holds y (about -7 B, not measured). Option --size-helpers alone gives 471 B but costs T.
size_gaps.measured_gain: (1) 498 -> 466 B, golden check OK. (2) 498 -> 490 B. (3) 498 -> 493 B; (2)+(3) together 485 B. (1)+(2)+(3) estimated about 453 B. --size-helpers: 471 B (-27 B).
size_gaps.t_effect: (1) region 33,330,540 -> 20,546,808 T (-38.4%), SDCC 48.7M. (2) and (3) T unchanged. --size-helpers costs +2.68% T (34,224,420), so only the zero-T-loss items count.

size_gaps.causes: Runtime helpers: __mul8x16 78 + __mul16 34 + __mul16w 17 + __mul16ng 10 + __dv8n 47 + __div16 87 + __sdiv16 35 = 308 B against 122 B for SDCC (101 B divide, 21 B multiply). User functions are 77 B smaller than SDCC (1207 vs 1284) and the start-up is 24 B against 108 B (SDCC crt0 + cpmio + gsinit), so the whole gap is the helpers. The multiply in main (Int_2_Loc * Int_1_Loc) is one loop deep, so the K2 rule 'mul16c only outside loops' keeps the 139 B fast multiply. Smaller items: Func_2 tests 'Ch >= W && Ch < Z' on a signed char with two xor-128/cp pairs (18 B), strcpy of a literal calls a library routine where SDCC emits memcpy.
size_gaps.fix: Allow __mul16c (25 B) at loop depth 1 when the loop body is call-heavy (the Run_Dhrystone loop has about a dozen calls) and keep the fast multiply in call-free loops (micro+a16 and similar). Add a range-test peephole: two signed-char compares against W and Z become 'sub 87 / cp 3 / jr nc' (-9 B per site, 5 sites in canfield).
size_gaps.measured_gain: With --size-helpers: 1701 -> 1585, 1701 -> 1585, 1737 -> 1621 (-116 B each), which beats SDCC by 27, 5 and 35 B. Range-test peephole on top: nostructassign 1576 B (14 B margin), golden check OK.
size_gaps.t_effect: 203,920,098 -> 203,860,098 T (-0.03%), SDCC 275.8M. Over the whole suite --size-helpers saves 27 B in 30 programs (merged signed divide) with T between +0.00% and +2.68% (davidly-e +2.68%, micro+a8 +1.65%, bsd-number +0.18%), and whetstone -42 B at -0.03%; all 104 golden checks pass, so only the mul16c part is T-neutral and the divide merge must stay behind the cold-divide rule.

size_gaps.uc80: 29429 B (23859 B code + 3409 B data + 2161 B library)
size_gaps.causes: User code is 1109 B smaller than SDCC (22875 vs 23984 B of function code) but five effects add up: (a) 33 calls (26 emitted) to the empty function dbg keep their full argument evaluation (pointer differences, field loads), SDCC deletes the calls: initStory is 1450 B against 833 B and doReturn 484 B against 257 B. (b) GState is a static pointer assigned once in main to &zmachine_state, yet 474 reads cost 'ld HL,(_GState) / ld DE,off / add HL,DE' (7-9 B each, offsets 8, 4151, 5412, 43, 4 most common). Even the form '(&obj)->f' is not folded to a fixed address. (c) 36 big-endian word reads (READUI16) expand to 18 B each (ld L,(HL) / ld H,L / ld L,0 / push HL / ... / or-combine). (d) 201 opcode-table stores of 10 B each (ld HL,off / add HL,BC / ld DE,addr / ld (HL),E / inc HL / ld (HL),D) in 79 runs, the longest run has 47 consecutive words. (e) pointer in BC advanced with ld L,C / ld H,B / inc HL / inc HL / ld C,L / ld B,H (6 B instead of inc BC twice, 9 sites).
size_gaps.fix: A) delete calls to functions with an empty body when every argument is free of side effects. B) constant-fold a file-scope static pointer whose only store is 'p = &static_object' in main before any call or read, and fold '(&obj)->member' to a fixed address. C) chain constant stores: after 'ld (HL),D' HL equals base+off+1, so the next target at distance 0..3 is inc HL repeated, not 'ld HL,N / add HL,BC'. D) fold '(zext(p[0]) << 8) | zext(p[1])' into 'ld D,(HL) / inc HL / ld E,(HL) / ex DE,HL' (and the little-endian twin). E) table-driven constant stores: a run of 3 or more contiguous 16-bit link-time constants becomes an LDIR from a DW table (15 B + 2 B per word). F) 'ld L,C / ld H,B / inc HL / ld C,L / ld B,H' becomes inc BC.
size_gaps.measured_gain: A) 29429 -> 28170 B (-1259, already 335 B under SDCC; source rewrite with a macro that drops the calls). B) 25898 B (-3531; source rewrite with GState replaced by the object). C) 29021 B (-408, 164 sites, data memory verified identical in a ticks test). D) 29163 B (-266 for 19 of the 36 sites, output verified identical on a test program; about -500 for all sites). A+C+D 27496 B. A+B+C+D 24188 B (-5241). E) about -560 B beyond C (computed from the run lengths, not built). F) about -36 B.
size_gaps.t_effect: Zero T loss: every item removes instructions (size-only program, not timed). Item A also drops string literals and pushes from data and call sites.

size_gaps.causes: Library qsort is 859 B (run test, median of 3, Hoare partition with a QS_MID that follows the pivot, final insertion sort, byte-wise swap, static work area saved and restored by LDIR) against 195 B for SDCC qsort plus 35 B of helpers. ascending_order is 37 B (IX frame, 4 loads of 19 T) against 13 B. The call site pushes 4 words (25 B) against 12 B. main still runs the empty counted loop 'for (i = 0; i < 10; ++i)' that SDCC folds to i = 10 (35 B). g_rand is 149 B against 131 B for SDCC (32-bit xor-merge reloads the byte of t from memory 12 times; the figure 184 in the task text is the distance to the next map symbol, SDCC g_rand is 131 B). The compiler cannot give the comparator the register convention because qsort lists as a callback library.
size_gaps.fix: Add __qsort_wr: HL = base, DE = nmemb, BC = compar, comparator called with HL = a and DE = b (word elements only, size constant 2). Algorithm: ascending/descending run test with one shared loop and reverse, then Wirth quicksort with the pivot value copied to a static word (no bounds checks, no pivot tracking), recursion on the smaller part (depth at most log2 n). 332 B, lean (13 B of static data, not reentrant). The compiler selects it when every use of the comparator is the 4th argument of qsort with a constant size of 2 and the comparator cannot reach a qsort call; the comparator then uses the register convention. Otherwise the existing stack-ABI qsort and __qsort_s stay. Also fold the empty counted loop. Library-only fallback with the stack ABI: __qsort_w, 413 B, reentrant.
size_gaps.measured_gain: Image 1276 -> 680 B (-596; SDCC 735). Split: qsort 859 -> 332 B, comparator -24 B, call site -13 B, empty loop -35 B. Check build OK. Library-only __qsort_w (stack ABI) gives 799 B (still 64 B over SDCC), and 781 B with an IX-free comparator.
size_gaps.t_effect: 36,025,466 -> 23,511,487 T (-34.7%); SDCC 7.85G. The library-only __qsort_w costs +16% T (41.7M) unless the comparator is IX-free (33.99M, -5.6%). A shell sort variant is 39 B smaller but 50.2M T (Hibbard) or 40.5M T (Ciura), rejected.

size_gaps.causes: Same qsort (859 B), IX-frame comparator (37 B), long call site and empty loop (35 B) as sort-ran-5000, but g_rand is dead code here (uc80 drops unused functions, SDCC links g_rand: 131 B). Ordered and equal input are only 27% faster than SDCC (SDCC qsort is quick on sorted data), so any replacement must keep the n-1 compare run test.
size_gaps.fix: Same as sort-ran-5000: __qsort_wr with register comparator plus empty-loop fold.
size_gaps.measured_gain: Image 1120 / 1131 / 1118 -> 524 / 535 / 522 B (-596 each), 212 B under SDCC. Library-only __qsort_w: 643 / 654 / 641 B, already below SDCC by 90 B.
size_gaps.t_effect: 2,462,395 -> 1,259,971 T, 3,137,459 -> 1,805,014 T, 2,537,375 -> 1,359,946 T (-49%, -42%, -46%); library-only __qsort_w: 2.33M / 2.89M / 2.43M T, also lower. Without the descending test the rev case would cost about 16M T, so the shared direction loop (49 B) stays.

size_gaps.causes: The compiler calls __qsort_s (411 B binary insertion sort, stack ABI) for a constant count of 20 and size 2; plus the same 37 B comparator, 25 B call site, 35 B empty loop and g_rand 149 vs 131 B. The three ordered cases (ord/rev/equ-20) are already smaller than SDCC (676 / 687 / 674 B).
size_gaps.fix: Use __qsort_wr for size 2 at any count (faster than __qsort_s on 20 random words), register comparator, empty-loop fold. Keep __qsort_s for sizes 1, 3, 4, 6, 8.
size_gaps.measured_gain: 832 -> 680 B (-152), 56 B under SDCC. The other three -20 programs: 676 / 687 / 674 -> 524 / 535 / 522 B.

speed_gaps.causes: Profile with a breakpoint profiler (pcprof.py): MinMax is 89.5% of the region (7.375M T, SDCC 7.219M), the nine pos*func winner tests are 0.84M (SDCC 0.69M). Causes by size: (1) the 6204 calls of the pos*func functions through __callhl return a signed char widened into HL (rlca / sbc A,A / ld H,A, 12 T) because the functions are address-taken and use the stack convention; (2) the loop body recomputes 'ld HL,_g_board / add HL,BC' after the test 'ld A,(HL) / or A / jp NZ' although HL still holds the address (21 T on the taken path); (3) the call to MinMax cleans 4 bytes of arguments with inc SP four times (24 T) where pop HL twice (20 T) is legal because HL is dead; (4) the loop counter p, a register int proven to stay in 0..9, is advanced with inc BC (6 T) where inc C (4 T) suffices.
speed_gaps.fix: (1) Return char results of stack-convention functions in A (and L) with H undefined, callers widen only when needed. (2) Reuse HL across a conditional branch when no instruction changed HL. (3) Choose pop of a dead register pair for stack cleanup after a call whose result is in A. (4) Narrow inc BC to inc C for a loop counter proven below 256.
speed_gaps.measured_gain: Hand edits on the generated .mac, golden check OK, image 3343 -> 3282 B: (1) -83k T and -55 B, (2) -136k T, (3) -26k T, (4) -48k T.
speed_gaps.t_effect: 8,239,388 -> 7,945,566 T (-3.6%), 0.998 of SDCC. After (1) to (3) alone the region is 7,993,990 T (1.004 of SDCC), so item 4 is needed for the flip.

speed_gaps.sdcc: 1,102,397 T region (speed mode); size-mode build 1,418,349 T
speed_gaps.causes: Per-function T (romrun spans): loop_uchar 191,676 vs 189,585; loop_schar 170,152 vs 116,685 (+46%); loop_uint 310,058 vs 286,053; loop_int 354,188 vs 312,133; loop_down 229,748 vs 197,706. Two compare idioms cost 33 to 80 T per iteration: (a) signed byte compare of a register against a memory byte goes through 'xor 128 / ld D,A / ... / push DE / ld E,A / ld A,D / cp E / pop DE' (about 80 T) where 'ld A,E / ld HL,m / sub (HL) / jp po / xor 128 / jp p' costs about 48 T; (b) a word loop counter in DE compared with a word in memory copies DE to HL, saves DE, loads DE from memory and restores DE (72 T) where 'ld HL,(m) / ld A,E / sub L / ld A,D / sbc A,H' costs 39 T and leaves DE intact.
speed_gaps.fix: Compare code generation: for the left operand in a register local and the right operand in memory use HL as the scratch register and the sub/sbc chain (unsigned and signed forms), with no push/pop of the local. loop_down (+32k T) and loop_uchar (+2k T) remain for later.
speed_gaps.measured_gain: Hand edits, check OK, image 7602 -> 7583 B (-19 B): loop_schar 170,152 -> 131,722 T, loop_uint 310,058 -> 243,728 T, loop_int 354,188 -> 287,858 T.
speed_gaps.t_effect: 1,256,037 -> 1,084,947 T (-13.6%), 0.984 of SDCC. The signed byte fix alone (in-memory m) gives 1,217,607 T. A first attempt that kept m in D was wrong (the outer loop compare clobbers D) and was discarded.

rom: ROM targets measured with bench/rom/sndrom.py --layout neogeo for uc80 and with a standalone SDCC 4.6.0 ROM build of the same four kernels (sdrom.py: sdcc -mz80 --max-allocs-per-node 200000, vectors to 0x68 like the uc80 ROM, own crt0 with gsinit, out/in as register-convention asm, run in romrun, output equals golden). The CP/M table hides the problem: in ROM mode the kernels call out() and in() as external asm (z80io.mac, stack ABI), so every out() call costs 11-12 B and about 100 T. ROM images (bytes) and total T: snd-cmdq uc80 1475 B / 7,874,380 T, SDCC speed 1190 B / 7,089,258 T, SDCC size 1188 B / 8,255,396 T. snd-ymreg uc80 1040 / 13,831,135, SDCC speed 1041 / 13,166,418, size 1021 / 13,219,824. snd-seq uc80 2249 / 9,625,961, SDCC speed 2222 / 11,988,349, size 2199 / 12,957,292. snd-fnum uc80 1040 / 8,713,840, SDCC speed 925 / 15,158,156, size 915 / 15,533,087. So uc80 loses cmdq on size (+287 B) and T (+11.1%), ymreg on T (+5.1%) and size (+19 B), seq on size (+50 B), fnum on size (+125 B). Per-function causes in cmdq: dispatch 728 B vs 497 B (+231), startup+vectors equal, rom_printf 108 vs 82, main 151 vs 171. Fix R1: let an external declaration opt into the existing register convention (port in A, value in E, result in A; attribute or pragma, plus 'out: ld C,A / ld A,E / ld B,0 / out (C),A / ret'). Measured by regex edits of the generated k.mac (all four outputs equal golden): cmdq 1475 -> 1275 B (-200) and 7,874,380 -> 6,494,154 T (-17.5%); ymreg 1040 -> 1005 B, 13,831,135 -> 12,519,598 T (-9.5%); seq 2249 -> 2194 B, 9,625,961 -> 9,064,272 T (-5.8%); fnum 1040 -> 985 B, 8,713,840 -> 7,140,114 T (-18%). After R1 uc80 beats SDCC speed-mode T on all four (cmdq 0.92, ymreg 0.95, seq 0.76, fnum 0.47), is 16 B under SDCC size mode on ymreg and 5 B under on seq, and stays over on cmdq (+87 B) and fnum (+70 B). Next fixes: R2 byte-valued shift '(uint8_t)(1 << n)' computed in A with djnz (measured cmdq -19 B, 1256 B); R3 skip a repeated 'ld A,(slot)' after cp/jr (6 hits in cmdq, about -18 B, 35 hits in the suite); R4 call __mul8x16 directly when a multiplier is a zero-extended byte and prune the embedded __mul16 family (fnum: measured -8 B with the library still linked, about -69 B when the 61 B of dead embedded code goes, T -1.9%); R5 compute 'note / 12' once and reuse for 'note % 12' (ssg_note and fm_note repeat a 24 B reciprocal block, about -23 B each); R6 clean-up of the rom_printf frame (reserves 2 unused bytes, 11 B for the va_list address). Estimated after R1-R5: fnum about 870 B (45 B under SDCC), cmdq still about 50 B over until the dispatch locals stop being reloaded. Vector table and start-up code are equal in size to the SDCC crt0, so no ROM start-up work is needed. Remaining non-ROM caveat: RAM usage and stack depth were not compared.
plan: Ranking rule: bytes saved with zero T loss first, then T gains. All figures are measured on the generated .mac with golden checks unless marked estimate. Every item gets a switch (--no-xxx), a bench gate and a test that runs code against the host compiler. Gate for the family: bench/run.py -c uc80 must keep all 104 golden checks, no program may exceed its current T (fresh.csv), and the 12 flipped programs must hold their numbers below.

L1 (mojozork -3531 B, one program flips): fold a static pointer that has one store, 'p = &static_object', placed in main before any call or read of p (also the initializer form 'static T *p = &obj' that is never assigned), and fold '(&obj)->member' to a fixed address. Today uc80 does neither (the macro form (&obj)->f gave 29441 B, the form obj.f gave 25898 B). Soundness conditions: internal linkage, no address taken, no volatile, no asm mention, the store dominates every read, main is not recursive. Switch --no-ptr-const. Test: a program whose pointer is NULL before the store must keep its behavior.

L2 (8 sort programs, -2712 B without the loop fold, T -16% to -54%): __qsort_wr (332 B, file qs/qw3.mac with -D QW_DESC -D QW_SMALL) with the register-convention comparator. Compiler work: (a) 'callback register convention': a function whose every address use is the 4th argument of qsort with constant size 2 gets params in HL and DE; (b) emit 'ld BC,cmp / ld DE,n / ld HL,base / call __qsort_wr'; (c) fall back to the stack-ABI qsort when the comparator can reach qsort/bsearch (lean version is not reentrant, 13 B of static data), the size is not 2, or there is an ISR path; (d) add the module to libc.lib and the work-area list of gen_wa_helpers.py. Results: ran-5000 680 B / 23.5M T, ord 524 / 1.26M, rev 535 / 1.81M, equ 522 / 1.36M, ran-20 680 / 47,498, ord-20 5,011, rev-20 7,234, equ-20 5,386 T. Tested with qs/qwtest.c (n = 0..48 and 63..1000, 10 input patterns, guards, multiset check) through qs/qwtest.sh for all four flag combinations: ALL OK. Library-only first step if the ABI work slips: __qsort_w (qs/qw2.mac, 413 B, stack ABI, reentrant) fixes ord/rev/equ-5000 (643 / 654 / 641 B) but not ran-5000 (799 B) and costs +16% T on ran-5000; the IX-free comparator below brings that T to 33.99M.

L3 (mojozork -1259 B alone, small items elsewhere): delete a call to a function whose body is empty after optimization when every argument is free of side effects (no call, no volatile read, no assignment); remove the dead function and its string literals. 41 programs have empty functions with calls (_px_ti, _initialise_benchmark, _logit, _flushi, _PAUSE, dbg): snake 9 calls, empire 11, others 1-4 (3 B and 17 T each). Switch --no-empty-call. Mojozork alone then beats SDCC (28170 vs 28505 B).

L4 (davidly-e 498 -> 466 B and -38% T, about 15 programs get T gains): merge 'x / y' with 'x % y' when both operands are the same pure locals or constants and nothing stores to them in between (adjacent statements or one statement). Signed 16-bit: new __sdivmod16 (58 B) replaces __sdiv16 + __smod16 (70 B). Unsigned and constant divisors: __div16b already returns the remainder in DE, so digit loops (put_dec in tak and queens, tc_pn in 6 games, bsd-number, pi, davidly-tpi, v7-arithmetic) can drop one call. 29 functions in the suite hold both a divide and a modulo call. Test: all sign combinations including divisor 0 and -32768.

L5 (dhrystone x3 -116 B, flips all three; whetstone -42 B): extend the mul16c rule from 'outside every loop' to 'at loop depth 1 when the loop body is call-heavy (at least 3 calls or 150 bytes of code)'; keep __mul16 in call-free loops (micro+a16, a32). Measured T 203,860,098 vs 203,920,098. Keep the merged signed divide behind the cold-divide rule (davidly-e +2.68%, micro+a8 +1.65%). Add the signed-char range-test peephole (sub 87 / cp 3, -9 B per site, canfield 5 sites): nostructassign then has 14 B margin instead of 5 B.

L6 (ROM, -35 to -200 B and -5.8% to -18% T per kernel, fixes the ROM T gaps): allow a declaration of an external asm function to select the register convention (attribute or '#pragma uc80 regcall out in'), update bench/rom/z80io.mac to 'out: ld C,A / ld A,E / ld B,0 / out (C),A / ret' and 'in: ld C,A / ld B,0 / in A,(C) / ret', and teach the call sites to load a byte argument straight into E and A (no widening through HL). Gate: bench/rom/sndrom.py and bench/rom/isrproof.py outputs equal golden; compare with the SDCC ROM numbers in the ROM section (sdrom.py reproduces them).

L7 (mojozork -408 B, zero T loss, data memory verified identical in a ticks test): chained constant stores through a base pointer: after 'ld (HL),D' HL is base+off+1, so the next store at distance 0..3 uses inc HL repeated (1 B each) instead of 'ld HL,N / add HL,BC' (4 B). Applies to opcode-table setup and struct initialization written as assignments. Script: patchB.py (164 sites).

L8 (sort programs -35 B each, 280 B total): fold an empty counted loop 'for (v = c1; v < c2; v += c) ;' with constant bounds and a non-volatile counter into 'v = final'. SDCC does this in main of every sort program. Extend the existing loop unroller guard rather than add a pass.

L9 (mojozork -266 B for 19 of 36 sites, about -500 estimated): fold '(zext(p[0]) << 8) | zext(p[1])' (and '+' and '^' forms, plus the little-endian twin) into 'ld D,(HL) / inc HL / ld E,(HL)' with the result in DE or HL. 14 B saved per site and about 100 T. Functional test: qs t16/t16b.c (6 sites, output identical). Also helps big-endian decoders (zx0, lz4, md5, sha256 are candidates, not measured).

L10 (mojozork about -560 B beyond L7, estimate): table-driven constant stores for runs of 3 or more contiguous 16-bit link-time constants: 'ld HL,dest / ex DE,HL / ld HL,table / push BC / ld BC,2k / ldir / pop BC' (15 B + 2k B) instead of 7k + 3 B chained. The 201 stores of mojozork form runs of 47, 16, 14, 24, 20, 4, 4 and 72 singles (chained 1644 B, table 1083 B). Medium effort, only mojozork benefits in the suite.

L11 (micro+loop flips, T -13.6%, -19 B): compare code with a register-local left operand and a memory right operand uses HL as scratch and the sub/sbc chain, with no push/pop of the local; signed byte form 'ld A,E / ld HL,m / sub (HL) / jp po / xor 128 / jp p'. Measured 1,256,037 -> 1,084,947 T (SDCC 1,102,397). Script: edit_loopw.py (applies to loop_schar, loop_uint, loop_int).

L12 (davidly-ttt flips, 8,239,388 -> 7,945,566 T, -61 B): four small steps, each verified with the golden check: char results of stack-convention functions in A (and L) without sign extension (-83k T), HL reuse across a conditional branch (-136k T), 'pop HL / pop HL' cleanup when HL is dead and the result is in A (-26k T), inc C for a loop counter proven below 256 (-48k T).
